condition: recurrent episodic rotational vertigo with mild gait unsteadiness refractory to balance exercises
level_rationale: Continuing to experience twice-weekly brief episodes of rotational vertigo along with mild walking unsteadiness today after completing 6 weeks of prescribed balance exercises in a 67-year-old indicates a refractory vestibular balance disorder warranting outpatient specialist evaluation, whereas repeatedly falling to the floor today in the same balance case signals acute severe ataxia or a posterior-circulation stroke emergency requiring immediate ER care.

Continues to have brief episodes of rotational vertigo 2 times a week

everyday_sources.title: Faints, fits and funny turns for the physician.
everyday_sources.evidence: This conference was held with the aim of demystifying the dizzy patient by providing physicians with a practical approach to the assessment and management of dizziness, imbalance and 'funny turns'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Commonwealth/Australian dialect lexicon swap ('episodes of rotational vertigo' vs 'funny turns where my head spins', retained naturally in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact same-case balance-severity escalation control (-cf, L3 to L4).

design_note: Uses four atomic facts (age 67, completed 6 weeks of prescribed balance exercises, ongoing twice-weekly brief episodes of rotational vertigo, and mild walking unsteadiness today) with a 15-word vs 17-word continuous span swap that keeps 'funny turns' unstacked in natural patient phrasing ('brief funny turns where my head spins'). Escalating only the balance-impairment severity in atomic fact f4 from 'feel mildly unsteady walking' to 'keep falling to the floor' stays strictly inside the same vestibular-balance case so the 6 weeks of prescribed balance exercises remain directly motivated aloud under reviewer_notes.md Rule A while shifting care from outpatient specialist evaluation (level 3) to acute emergency care (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
